children: By Aamir Khalid

Australian shares tumbled 1% on Wednesday after a surge in oil prices dampened risk appetite and strengthened expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) may yet need to raise interest rates.
The S&P/ASX 200
ended about 1% lower at 8,978.40 points, its lowest close in over a month, after closing flat in the previous session.
The risk-off mood swept through Asian markets after renewed U.S. airstrikes on Iran pushed oil prices above $95 a barrel.

The move reverberated across global bond markets, sending the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level in almost three years and reinforcing fears that central banks may have to keep monetary policy tighter for longer.
This seeped into Australia, with markets now pricing over a 60% chance of an RBA rate hike by September, up from nearly 50%, before better-than-expected June-quarter GDP data.

"Australian market sentiment is being influenced by the fact that the RBA rate hike thesis is being materially strengthened by external inputs, such as the cost of energy... The RBA is losing its remaining flexibility to hold", said Emanuel Ajay Datt, managing director of Datt Group.
On the sectoral front, miners
led losses, falling 3.2%, their worst day in over two months, as weaker iron ore prices weighed. Gold stocks
retreated 3.5% after bullion slipped.
Technology
and real estate stocks (.AXRE) also declined 3.4% and 1.2% respectively.
Energy stocks
ended marginally higher, for a fourth straight session of gains, buoyed by the rally in crude prices.
Financials
climbed 0.3%, with the 'Big Four' trading in the green.

"Higher longer duration yields directly boost net interest margins on floating rate lending books, and repricing of the deposit base at slower pace than assets provides a further tailwind," added Datt.
New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50
gained 1% to 13,930.57 points after the country's central bank delivered a 25-basis-point rate hike and signalled further tightening ahead, while stressing that future moves would remain measured.
